outcome: No accepted resolution found as of 11 Oct 2026. The only general-case proof claims since 26 Jan 2024 are Mihail Cocos's arXiv:1504.04852, revised 31 Mar 2025 to 6 Dec 2025 (v4 to v12) on a new route; nothing in the sources shows a referee, journal acceptance or public expert check. Two in-window results are restricted cases: Hanwen Liu's arXiv:2509.01176 (compact Hessian manifolds, Sep 2025, v7 Jun 2026) and Cocos's arXiv:2510.09648 (affine-orthogonal manifolds, Oct 2025, presented as evidence). The Cocos v4 acknowledgement is the only AI-system credit found, and it is for technical calculations.
problem_asks: Statement (Wikipedia, Jan 2024): 'Chern's conjecture (affine geometry) that the Euler characteristic of a compact affine manifold vanishes.' Parts: (1) For every compact affine manifold M (a smooth manifold whose coordinate changes are affine maps, equivalently a flat torsion-free affine connection on TM), in every dimension, with any holonomy, complete or incomplete: (2) the Euler characteristic chi(M) equals 0. It is one universal claim with no separate sub-parts. Two readings to keep visible: 'compact' is read in the literature as closed (compact without boundary), and the Wikipedia wording does not say whether manifolds with boundary are included. Closed odd-dimensional manifolds have chi = 0 automatically (Poincare duality), so the content of the claim lies in even dimensions; the odd-dimensional part is not what remains open.

events.what_happened: Mihail Cocos posted arXiv:1504.04852 on 19 Apr 2015 as 'Pointwise metric compatible connections and a conjecture of Chern on affine manifolds'. The v1 abstract defines the Euler form for a point-wise metric connection and says: 'Using this construction we prove that every closed,oriented,affine manifold has zero Euler Poincare characteristic.' v3 (6 Aug 2015) is retitled 'Quasi-metric connections and a conjecture of Chern on affine manifolds'; its abstract defines the Euler form for a general linear connection satisfying a minor compatibility condition with a given metric and says 'every closed,affine manifold has zero Euler characteristic'. Both claim the full conjecture. The first public written argument is this 2015 version, which predates the frozen Wikipedia revision.
events.revisions: v1 19 Apr 2015 (title 'Pointwise metric compatible connections...'); v2 1 Aug 2015; v3 6 Aug 2015 (title 'Quasi-metric connections...'); v4 31 Mar 2025 (title 'Proof of Chern conjecture for flat affine manifolds'); v5 11 Apr 2025; v6 28 Apr 2025; v7 13 May 2025; v8 3 Jun 2025; v9 16 Jun 2025; v10 13 Jul 2025; v11 7 Sep 2025; v12 6 Dec 2025 (html title 'On Polarized Pfaffians and the Euler Characteristic of Flat Affine Manifolds'). The v4 onward route is separately recorded as cocos-2025-revised-route.
events.delivers: As claimed in the 2015 abstracts: the full conjecture for closed affine manifolds (v1: closed, oriented), via an Euler form defined for connections that are only pointwise or quasi metric-compatible. Not checked: the PDFs of v1 and v3 were binary and unreadable in my fetches, so I read only the abstracts and the arXiv metadata.
events.remains: If the claim held, nothing of problem_asks. The claim covers all closed affine manifolds as stated in the abstracts.
events.time_since_posted: About 11 years 6 months to 11 Oct 2026. No referee, journal publication or public expert reading found in any search. The Wikipedia article as fetched does not mention Cocos.
events.doubts: (a) Known obstacle: Chern-Weil and Gauss-Bonnet give chi = 0 only when the flat connection is compatible with a metric, and not every flat torsion-free connection on TM admits one (Wikipedia, Klingler, Arias Abad-Velez Vasquez). The 2015 argument reduces the general case to metric-compatible connections, which is the step the obstacle concerns. I could not read the 2015 text to check how that step is handled. (b) The author's own versions do not describe the 2015 argument as the final proof: the title and abstract changed in 2025 and the route changed (see cocos-2025-revised-route). (c) Two general-case claims by others in this area (Feng-Zhang 2016, Ge 2020) were withdrawn for errors, so the field has a record of failed general proofs of this kind.
events.direction: Claims the conjecture in full: chi(M) = 0 for every closed affine manifold. Direction matches the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: AMS meeting abstract 1114-58-130 by Mihail Cocos (Weber State University), 'On a possible proof of Chern conjecture for affine manifolds', received 20 Aug 2015. Per the search-result summary, it proposes a route to the conjecture based on the local Riemannian character of affine manifolds and is described as a proposal, not a complete proof. The PDF returned HTTP 403 when I tried to open it, so these details are from search metadata only.
events.delivers: Per the search summary only: a proposed approach to the full conjecture, explicitly not a proof. Establishes nothing on its own.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.time_since_posted: About 11 years 2 months to 11 Oct 2026. No engagement found.
events.doubts: Source not opened (HTTP 403). The date is the 'received' date from metadata, not a talk date.
events.direction: Proposes a route toward the conjecture (direction consistent with it). No object.

events.what_happened: Huitao Feng and Weiping Zhang posted arXiv:1603.07248 on 23 Mar 2016 as 'Superconnections and affine manifolds'. The v1 abstract uses the Mathai-Quillen superconnection construction of the Thom class to show that the Euler characteristic of a compact affine manifold is zero and says: 'This solves an old conjecture of S. S. Chern.' v3 (20 Sep 2017) is retitled 'Flat vector bundles and open coverings'; its abstract states a counting formula for the Euler number of a flat vector bundle of rank 2n over a closed 2n-manifold in terms of vertices of transversal open coverings. The v3 comment says: 'An error in the previous version was found.' and 'The Chern conjecture remains open'. Zhang gave a Peking University seminar on this work on 27 Apr 2017, which is after the 2016 write-up and so does not change the date.
events.revisions: v1 23 Mar 2016 ('Superconnections and affine manifolds'); v2 5 Sep 2016; v3 20 Sep 2017 ('Flat vector bundles and open coverings'; comment: 'Title changed. An error in the previous version was found.').
events.delivers: v1 as claimed: the full conjecture for compact affine manifolds. v3 (the later version): does not claim the conjecture; it proves a counting formula for the Euler number of flat vector bundles of rank 2n and states that the Chern conjecture remains open.
events.remains: v1: nothing claimed. v3: all of problem_asks.
events.time_since_posted: About 10 years 6 months to 11 Oct 2026; withdrawn in substance Sep 2017.
events.doubts: The author-stated error is not identified in the sources I could read. Wikipedia (as fetched) says: 'claimed to prove the conjecture in general case, but a serious flaw had been found, so the claim was thereafter retracted.' I found no journal retraction notice; the withdrawal is evidenced by the v3 arXiv comment and the Wikipedia statement.

withdrawn.what: Claim of a general proof in v1 and v2 (superconnection argument); v3 replaces it with a different counting result and says the Chern conjecture remains open.

events.direction: v1 claims the conjecture (chi = 0 for every compact affine manifold). v3 does not.

events.what_happened: Bruno Klingler, 'Chern's conjecture for special affine manifolds', Annals of Mathematics 186 (2017), 69-95. Proves the conjecture when the affine manifold also admits a parallel volume form. The abstract says: 'In this paper we prove Chern's conjecture in the case where X moreover admits a parallel volume form.' Journal dates: received 21 Apr 2015, revised 30 Mar 2016, accepted 8 Feb 2017, published online 31 May 2017. Wikipedia and a 2018 thesis date the result to 2015. I could not find the arXiv identifier or the exact first-posting date.
events.revisions: Journal: Annals 186(1) 2017, DOI 10.4007/annals.2017.186.1.2. First arXiv posting not located; year 2015 from Wikipedia and a thesis. Author-hosted PDF at hu-berlin.de was unreadable in my fetch.
events.delivers: The full conjecture restricted to special affine manifolds (those with a parallel volume form). Restriction: the parallel volume form. Silent on the non-special case.
events.remains: The general case of problem_asks, for affine manifolds that admit no parallel volume form.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal of record; referee names not public in my sources.
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper on 8 Feb 2017 and published it in volume 186, issue 1.

events.time_since_posted: About 11 years to Oct 2026, accepted and published 2017.
events.direction: Proves the conjecture for the special case: chi = 0 for special affine manifolds. Direction matches the conjecture in that case.

events.what_happened: Benzecri proved the conjecture for closed affine surfaces (dimension 2): a closed affine surface has chi = 0. Wikipedia dates this to 1955; Bucher, Connell and Lafont cite it as [Be60]. I did not open the original.
events.delivers: The conjecture in dimension 2 (closed affine surfaces).
events.remains: All dimensions 4 and up (and even dimensions generally).

checked_by.qualification: Topologist who characterised flat rank-two bundles over surfaces.
checked_by.what_they_did: Gave a second proof and generalised the surface case to plane bundles over surfaces (1957/1958 per Wikipedia).

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in dimension 2.

events.what_happened: Milnor's 1957/1958 work: a second proof of the surface case, and inequalities characterising oriented rank-two bundles over a surface that admit a flat connection. These show the torsion-free hypothesis is not needed in dimension 2. Taken from Wikipedia and secondary summaries; the original was not opened.
events.revisions: Wikipedia gives 1957 for the second proof and the inequalities are dated 1958 in secondary summaries.
events.delivers: Surfaces, including plane bundles over surfaces.
events.remains: Dimensions 4 and up.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in dimension 2.

events.what_happened: Kostant and Sullivan proved the conjecture for complete affine manifolds, by an argument on the monodromy (per Wikipedia and the Arias Abad-Velez Vasquez lecture notes). The original was not opened.
events.delivers: The conjecture for complete affine manifolds.
events.remains: Incomplete affine manifolds, unless covered by other special cases.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the complete case.

events.what_happened: Hirsch and Thurston proved the conjecture for incomplete affine manifolds whose holonomy group is a finite extension of a free product of amenable groups. Per the Cocos reference list and the Choi summary. The original was not opened.
events.delivers: Incomplete affine manifolds with holonomy a finite extension of a free product of amenable groups.
events.remains: Incomplete affine manifolds outside that holonomy class.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the amenable-holonomy class.

events.what_happened: Smillie showed that dropping the torsion-free condition breaks the conjecture: in each even dimension above 2 there are closed manifolds with nonzero Euler characteristic admitting a flat connection on their tangent bundle. Some sources date this to 1976. The connection in these examples has nonzero torsion, so they are not affine manifolds. Recorded as a discarded event: it is about a different object and does not contradict the conjecture as stated.
events.revisions: Dated 1976 by Goldman's survey and 1977 by Wikipedia and other sources.
events.delivers: Not about affine structures. Shows that a flat connection on TM with torsion is not enough for chi = 0.
events.remains: Not relevant: this does not bear on the torsion-free statement.
events.direction: Does not contradict the conjecture: the counterexamples are flat connections with nonzero torsion, not torsion-free affine structures.
events.object: Closed manifolds of even dimension at least 4 with nonzero Euler characteristic and a flat connection on their tangent bundle that is not torsion-free (Smillie's construction, per Cocos and Goldman summaries). Not explicit as I read it; no further detail obtained.

events.what_happened: Goldman and Hirsch: the conjecture for higher-rank irreducible locally symmetric manifolds (per Wikipedia). Not opened.
events.delivers: Higher-rank irreducible locally symmetric manifolds only.
events.remains: Everything outside that class.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in that class.

events.what_happened: H. Kim and H. Lee: Euler characteristic of projectively flat manifolds with amenable holonomy (Topology 40, 1991) and with amenable fundamental groups (Proc. AMS 118, 1993). Their route extends the amenable-holonomy result, including affine manifolds with amenable holonomy, by combinatorial methods. Known only from the Cocos reference list, search summaries and Wikipedia; not opened. Wikipedia spells the author Huyk Kim, Jo-Kim paper spells it Hyuk Kim.
events.revisions: 1993 Proc. AMS paper on the amenable fundamental group case (per Cocos's reference list).
events.delivers: Affine manifolds with amenable holonomy, and projectively flat manifolds with amenable fundamental group, per secondary summaries.
events.remains: Non-amenable holonomy.
events.doubts: Statements taken from secondary summaries; the abstracts were not read.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the amenable case.

events.what_happened: Suhyoung Choi: 'The Chern conjecture for affinely flat manifolds using combinatorial methods' (Springer, DOI 10.1023/A:1023664521970). Generalises Hirsch-Thurston to amenable groups amalgamated or HNN-extended over finite groups, and shows that an even-dimensional connected sum of K(pi,1)s with amenable fundamental groups admits no affine structure. Known from the KAIST record and search summaries; the paper was not opened. Dated 2002/2003 by different sources.
events.delivers: Amenable-holonomy class (amalgamated or HNN extensions over finite groups); connected sums of K(pi,1)s with amenable fundamental groups have no affine structure.
events.remains: Other holonomy classes.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the stated classes.

events.what_happened: Jo and Kim (2003): chi of an even-dimensional closed projectively flat manifold equals the total measure from a holonomy-invariant probability Borel measure on RP^n; hence closed affinely flat manifolds whose holonomy admits such a measure have chi = 0. Known only from a search summary; not opened.
events.delivers: Affine manifolds whose holonomy preserves an invariant probability measure on RP^n.
events.remains: Holonomy with no invariant probability measure.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in that class.

events.what_happened: Bucher and Gelander: the generalised Chern conjecture for closed manifolds locally a product of hyperbolic planes (or of surfaces), arXiv:0902.1215 (ID indicates February 2009). Wikipedia dates the result to 2011. The arXiv abstract was not opened; the title came from search results.
events.revisions: Wikipedia gives 2011; arXiv ID 0902 gives February 2009. Header reported as 19 Mar 2024 in one summary, which I could not confirm.
events.delivers: Closed manifolds locally a product of hyperbolic planes (or of surfaces): these admit no affine structure, so the conjecture holds there. Restricted class.
events.remains: All other closed affine manifolds.
events.doubts: Arxiv abstract not opened. The 2024 date in one summary likely reflects a later revision and is not a new result.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the locally-product class.

events.what_happened: Hester Pieters (2016): the conjecture for compact affine manifolds that are complex hyperbolic surfaces, per Wikipedia. The paper was not found in my searches.
events.delivers: Complex hyperbolic surfaces only.
events.remains: Other classes.
events.doubts: Only Wikipedia's mention; the primary source was not located.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in that class.

events.what_happened: Michelle Bucher, Chris Connell and Jean-Francois Lafont, 'Vanishing simplicial volume for certain affine manifolds' (arXiv:1610.00832, 4 Oct 2016; Proc. AMS 146 (2018)). The abstract says closed aspherical manifolds with an affine structure whose holonomy map is injective and contains a pure translation 'must have vanishing simplicial volume'. Consequence: chi = 0 in that class. The paper also answers a special case of a question of Luck. The abstract does not mention Euler characteristic or Chern.
events.revisions: arXiv 1610.00832 (4 Oct 2016); Proc. AMS 146(3), 2018, per search metadata.
events.delivers: Closed aspherical affine manifolds with injective holonomy containing a pure translation: simplicial volume zero, hence chi = 0. Restricted class; the Euler-characteristic consequence is in the published paper, per the Casali-Moraschini summary.
events.remains: Everything outside the injective-holonomy-with-translation class, including the general simplicial-volume conjecture of Bucher-Connell-Lafont and Luck.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society (refereed journal)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in Proc. AMS 146 (2018); journal page seen only in search metadata.

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in a restricted class (chi = 0 follows from vanishing simplicial volume).

events.what_happened: Jianquan Ge (Beijing Normal University) posted arXiv:2002.03105 on 8 Feb 2020, 'Proof of Chern's conjecture on affine manifolds'. Abstract: 'We prove an old conjecture of S. S. Chern that the Euler characteristic of a closed affine manifold equals to zero.' Theorem 1.1 states the same. v2 (27 Jul 2020) is marked withdrawn by the author. The v1 acknowledgements thank Weiping Zhang for 'taking his attention to the Chern conjecture' and thank Jiagui Peng and Zizhou Tang.
events.revisions: v1 8 Feb 2020; v2 27 Jul 2020 (withdrawn; comment: 'Although this paper is withdrawed now to avoid some misunderstanding, I'm still trying to overcome this error.').
events.delivers: Claimed: the full conjecture for closed affine manifolds. Withdrawn in v2.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, after withdrawal.
events.time_since_posted: About 6 years 8 months to Oct 2026; withdrawn Jul 2020. No public engagement beyond the v2 comment found.
events.doubts: The v2 comment names two errors: 'an error in the Hessian representation in Lemma 2.1' and 'a further error in the commutation of limits at the end of the proof'. The v1 text itself is not checked by me; the v1 PDF was unreadable in my fetch, and I read the HTML version only in part (it notes several steps as 'left to the readers' or 'not hard to show'). One search summary says a named mathematician (Andrea Clini) reported the Lemma 2.1 error; I could not confirm that from the arXiv page.

withdrawn.what: Full withdrawal of the general-case proof, with the author stating that errors were found and that the author is still working to overcome them.

events.direction: Claimed: chi = 0 for every closed affine manifold. Direction matches the conjecture as stated; the claim has been withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Fagui Li, 'A note on the Chern Conjecture in dimension four' (arXiv, 16 Apr 2021). Concerns closed minimal hypersurfaces with constant squared length of the second fundamental form in the sphere S^5 and concludes that they are isoparametric. This is Chern's conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces in spheres, a different problem sharing the name.
events.delivers: Nothing about affine manifolds. Different problem: minimal hypersurfaces in spheres.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, unchanged.
events.direction: Not about this problem.

events.what_happened: Alberto Casali and Marco Moraschini, 'Topological volumes of certain complete affine manifolds' (arXiv:2502.06303, 10 Feb 2025). Abstract: they estimate the amenable category of oriented closed connected complete affine manifolds whose fundamental group contains an infinite amenable normal subgroup, and deduce that all such manifolds have zero simplicial volume; this answers a question of Luck in the complete case. The abstract does not mention the Euler characteristic or the Chern conjecture. The paper's introduction, per a summary, still calls the general simplicial-volume statement a conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 10 Feb 2025; later versions not checked.
events.delivers: Vanishing simplicial volume for closed complete affine manifolds whose fundamental group contains an infinite amenable normal subgroup. Chern's conjecture for complete affine manifolds was already known (Kostant-Sullivan 1975), so this does not move the Euler-characteristic question.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, including the incomplete case and every case outside the amenable-normal-subgroup class.
events.time_since_posted: About 1 year 8 months to Oct 2026. No engagement found.
events.doubts: Only the abstract was read; the introduction statement about the general conjecture is from a search summary.
events.direction: Does not address chi = 0 in the stated form; relates to a simplicial-volume strengthening, in the complete case only.

events.what_happened: Cocos revised arXiv:1504.04852 from v4 (31 Mar 2025) to v12 (6 Dec 2025), changing title and route. The v4 html says: 'In this paper, we give the proof of the general case of the conjecture' and describes a one-parameter family of connections from the given flat connection to a Levi-Civita connection, built from locally metric connections, together with a rigidity theorem for holonomy groups (attributed to Cocos, Geom. Dedicata 2006), and then Stokes' theorem. The v4 abstract as fetched: 'We prove Chern's conjecture ... for compact flat affine manifolds' (html) or 'closed, finely flat manifold' (abs page); the two fetches disagree. v12 (html title 'On Polarized Pfaffians and the Euler Characteristic of Flat Affine Manifolds') has abstract 'We explore an approach to Chern's conjecture ... using polarized Pfaffians' but Theorem 4.2 states that any closed even-dimensional manifold with a flat affine connection has vanishing Euler characteristic.
events.revisions: v4 31 Mar 2025 (route change; first version carrying the new argument as far as the fetches show); v5 11 Apr 2025; v6 28 Apr 2025; v7 13 May 2025; v8 3 Jun 2025; v9 16 Jun 2025; v10 13 Jul 2025; v11 7 Sep 2025; v12 6 Dec 2025. Whether the 2025 route is the 2015 argument with changes, or a new argument, is not settled by my reading. Compare cocos-2015-general-claim.
events.delivers: Claimed: the full conjecture (chi = 0) for closed or compact flat affine manifolds. Restriction in the html abstract: flat affine manifolds (torsion-free flat connection on TM). The v12 abstract instead says 'We explore an approach'; the v12 html introduction says it gives a proof of the general case.
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim holds; the claim covers closed and compact flat affine manifolds in every dimension. Dependence on the rigidity theorem and on the local metrizability step is not checked.
events.time_since_posted: About 6 months since v4; about 19 months since the new route was first posted in 2025 (Oct 2026). No referee, publication, or public expert reading found in any search.
events.doubts: (a) Versions disagree on what is claimed: v12 abstract says 'explore an approach'; v12 introduction says 'the proof of the general case'. (b) The html title for v12 differs from the title on the unversioned abs page, which still shows 'Proof of Chern conjecture for flat affine manifolds' with v12 listed. (c) The key step of the v4 route is 'local metrizability' of the family of connections; the only acknowledgement in v4 credits DeepSeek Chat for technical calculations on exactly that (see ai). Those calculations are not described. (d) The route runs through metric-compatible connections, the step that the known obstacle (Gauss-Bonnet needs a compatible metric) concerns. (e) Earlier general claims in this area (Feng-Zhang 2016, Ge 2020) were withdrawn. (f) Keyword checks found no acknowledgement or AI disclosure in v5, v6, v7, v9, v11 or v12 (html); the v4 PDF was unreadable, so I could not check the PDF text of v4 directly. (g) Wikipedia's article (as fetched) does not cite Cocos.
events.direction: Claims the conjecture in full: chi = 0 for every closed or compact flat affine manifold. Direction matches the conjecture as stated.

systems.name: DeepSeek Chat
systems.what_it_did: Per the acknowledgement, assistance with technical calculations related to the local metrizability of the paper's one-parameter family of connections. The paper does not say which calculations were done, what was checked, or whether the results were used in the proof. Whether this is load-bearing is for the judging pass: it touches the key step of the v4 route but may be routine computation.
systems.basis_quote: We are thankful to DeepSeek Chat (DeepSeek, 2024) for assistance with technical calculations related to the local metrizability of our 1-1-parameter family of connections.

events.what_happened: Hanwen Liu (University of Warwick), arXiv:2509.01176, first posted 1 Sep 2025 as 'On Topology and Geometry of Hessian Manifolds', retitled 'On Topology of Compact Hessian Manifolds' in later versions; v7 is current (11 Jun 2026). The abstract states that the paper, 'by establishing novel fibration and splitting theorems, ... confirm[s] Chern's conjecture on the vanishing of the Euler characteristic for this class of affine manifolds', and the introduction says 'our work confirms Chern's longstanding 1955 conjecture in this particular setting'. It also gives classifications for complete Hessian surfaces and closed orientable Hessian 3-manifolds. Method per summary: sheaf cohomology of affine functions. The result covers compact Hessian manifolds only.
events.revisions: v1 1 Sep 2025; v2 9 Oct 2025; v3 15 Oct 2025; v4 20 Oct 2025; v5 3 Nov 2025; v6 18 Nov 2025; v7 11 Jun 2026 (current). Titles: v1 'On Topology and Geometry of Hessian Manifolds'; later 'On Topology of Compact Hessian Manifolds'. Numbering of the key proposition changes between versions (Prop 2.17 in earlier versions, Prop 4.3 in the later one, per a search summary).
events.delivers: Claimed: chi = 0 for every compact Hessian manifold (a Hessian manifold is an affine manifold with a metric locally the Hessian of a potential). Restriction: the Hessian class only. The general compact affine case is not addressed.
events.remains: All compact affine manifolds that are not Hessian (and not otherwise covered).
events.time_since_posted: About 13 months to Oct 2026. No referee, publication, or public expert reading found in any search.
events.doubts: Preprint, unrefereed, 49 pages, with several versions. The method goes through fibration and splitting theorems; I did not check them. Only the first 100,000 of about 172,000 characters of v6 were read in the keyword check, so the AI and acknowledgement check is incomplete for v6. The abstract's classification results for surfaces and 3-manifolds are separate claims.
events.direction: Claims the conjecture for compact Hessian manifolds: chi = 0 in that class. Direction matches the conjecture in that restricted class.

events.what_happened: Mihail Cocos, 'Affine-Orthogonal Manifolds and Deformation to Levi-Civita Connections' (arXiv:2510.09648, 6 Oct 2025, single version). Studies affine manifolds with a flat affine connection and a global Riemannian metric diagonal in local affine coordinates (close to Hessian manifolds); the Hopf manifold example admits a proper deformation of its flat connection to its Levi-Civita connection. Per the paper as summarised: 'such deformations force the Euler characteristic to vanish, providing evidence for Chern's conjecture', citing the author's earlier Theorem 2.3.
events.delivers: Restricted: for affine-orthogonal manifolds (flat affine connection with a global metric diagonal in affine coordinates, admitting a proper deformation to Levi-Civita), chi = 0. Described by the author as evidence for the conjecture, not a proof of it. Relies on the author's own earlier theorem.
events.remains: All affine manifolds without the affine-orthogonal structure, which is the general conjecture.
events.time_since_posted: About 1 year to Oct 2026. No engagement found.
events.doubts: Self-citation for the key theorem (Theorem 2.3 of the author's earlier work, which the author's own 2025 proof uses). Only the abstract page and the html keyword check were read.
events.direction: Evidence for the conjecture on a restricted class (chi = 0 for affine-orthogonal manifolds). Not a claim of the general case.

events.what_happened: Emmanuel Gnandi, 'The topology of 3-dimensional Hessian manifolds' (arXiv:2510.21050, v1 23 Oct 2025; v2 18 Feb 2026). Classifies compact orientable 3-dimensional Hessian manifolds as Seifert manifolds with trivial Euler number. Does not mention Chern's conjecture. Recorded as a discarded event: the Euler characteristic of closed 3-manifolds is zero for every manifold, so this bears on nothing here.
events.delivers: Nothing about Chern's conjecture; odd-dimensional case is automatic.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Not about this problem.

events.what_happened: Davide Dameno and Aaron J. Tyrrell, 'Topological and rigidity results for four-dimensional hypersurfaces in space forms' (arXiv:2603.03775, v1 4 Mar 2026; v2 29 Apr 2026). Mentions 'a famous conjecture by Chern and the so-called second pinching problem' as motivation. About minimal hypersurfaces in space forms; no affine manifolds. Recorded as a discarded event.

disputes.summary: No documented dispute. Three general-case claims have been posted: Cocos (first posted April 2015, then rewritten in 2025), Feng-Zhang (March 2016, withdrawn in substance Sept 2017), and Ge (Feb 2020, withdrawn July 2020). Ge's acknowledgements thank Weiping Zhang, who coauthored the Feng-Zhang work. The Cocos 2015 claim predates both. I found no exchange between the authors and no response from others in the sources.

summary:
Sources: Wikipedia's article (opened; as fetched it says the problem 'remains an unsolved mathematical problem' as of 2025, does not mention Cocos or Ge, and says the Feng-Zhang claim was 'thereafter retracted'); the arXiv pages for the relevant preprints (opened as abstracts and, where readable, as html); the Annals page for Klingler; and Proc. AMS metadata. The PDFs of the Cocos 2015 and 2025 versions, of Ge v1, and of Klingler's author PDF were binary in my fetches, so I did not read their full text.

What happened since 26 Jan 2024: the general conjecture was claimed proved in 2025 by Cocos, in a revised arXiv preprint that first appeared in 2015 and was rewritten from v4 (31 Mar 2025) onward. It is not refereed, I found no journal acceptance, no expert reading, and no later paper that accepts or refutes it. Two other in-window results are restricted cases: Liu (Sep 2025, v7 Jun 2026) on compact Hessian manifolds, and Cocos (Oct 2025) on affine-orthogonal manifolds, which the author presents only as evidence. Casali and Moraschini (Feb 2025) give vanishing simplicial volume for complete affine manifolds, which does not move the Euler-characteristic question, since the complete case was already known.

Close calls. (1) Whether the Cocos claim counts as a resolution. For: it is a complete, dated proof claim on the exact statement, and it has not been withdrawn. Against: it is unrefereed, its versions disagree on what is claimed (v12 abstract says 'explore an approach', v12 introduction says 'proof of the general case'), there is no uptake in ~11 years, and two earlier general claims in this area were withdrawn for errors. (2) Which Cocos date is the first written argument. Read literally, the 2015 arXiv v1 (19 Apr 2015) carries a general claim, so it predates the frozen revision; the 2025 route is a different argument, so I recorded it separately. Whether the 2025 route is the 2015 argument with changes is not settled by my reading. (3) Whether Liu's Hessian result moves the problem. It confirms the conjecture for a subclass, so it adds instances of a universal statement rather than changing the general claim; the judging pass should decide that.

AI involvement. The only AI-system credit I found is in Cocos's v4 html (31 Mar 2025), which thanks 'DeepSeek Chat (DeepSeek, 2024)' for 'assistance with technical calculations related to the local metrizability of our 1-1-parameter family of connections'. Two separate fetches confirmed the first part of the sentence; the tail was reported by the fetch tool and I could not check it character by character. Keyword checks of v5, v6, v7, v9, v11 and v12 found no DeepSeek or other AI credit, and the v12 html and v4 html disagree with each other only on the abstract, not on the acknowledgement. The authors do not say whether the calculations were used in the proof. No other AI credit for this problem: I searched for AI and this conjecture across lab announcements, tracker sites, news and the arXiv results, and found none. Nearby but different: an August 2026 claim credits 'Claude' (via Levent Alpoge) with a complex structure on S^6, which is the Hopf problem, not this one; a crypto news aggregator credits an 'Odin' agent with a positive-curvature metric on S^3 x S^3 and ties it to a Hopf-type sign conjecture, but I found no primary source and no mention of 'Odin' as an AI system, so I did not record it.

What I could not establish: whether any version of the Cocos argument is correct; whether Liu or Cocos (2025) has been cited by anyone outside the authors' own work (the self-citation in Cocos 2510.09648 is noted); the exact arXiv first-posting date of Klingler's special case; and Benzecri, Kostant-Sullivan, Hirsch-Thurston, Goldman-Hirsch, Kim-Lee, Choi, Jo-Kim and Pieters are recorded from Wikipedia and secondary summaries, not from the primary papers.
competing_reading: Read the Cocos 2025 preprint as a claimed resolution of the general conjecture that has simply not been examined yet: a complete argument on the exact statement, on arXiv since 2015 with versions through Dec 2025, with no published rebuttal, and the problem's status is therefore 'claimed, not verified'. Against this, the claim has the same shape as the two withdrawn general claims (Feng-Zhang, Ge), it changes its route and title across versions, it hedges in v12's abstract, and the 2025 rewrite credits a general-purpose chatbot with calculations on the key step, so a judge could reasonably treat it as unreliable and the problem as still open. Between the two readings the record gives the same facts; the difference is whether no-uptake for about 11 years, and the author's own hedging, count against the claim.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A journal of record accepting one of the Cocos versions, or a named expert's public verification or rebuttal of the local metrizability step and the rigidity theorem it uses. (2) The arXiv v4-to-v12 change log or the author's own statement of what changed and whether the 2015 argument is still claimed. (3) The full text of the DeepSeek-assisted calculations or a statement of what they checked. (4) Citations of Cocos 2025 or Liu 2025 by independent authors, and whether those authors still call the general problem open. (5) The 2026 state of the Wikipedia article, which as fetched says 'as of 2025' and does not mention Cocos.

event.what_happened: Hanwen Liu (University of Warwick), arXiv:2509.01176, first posted 1 Sep 2025 as 'On Topology and Geometry of Hessian Manifolds', retitled 'On Topology of Compact Hessian Manifolds' in later versions; v7 is current (11 Jun 2026). The abstract states that the paper, 'by establishing novel fibration and splitting theorems, ... confirm[s] Chern's conjecture on the vanishing of the Euler characteristic for this class of affine manifolds', and the introduction says 'our work confirms Chern's longstanding 1955 conjecture in this particular setting'. It also gives classifications for complete Hessian surfaces and closed orientable Hessian 3-manifolds. Method per summary: sheaf cohomology of affine functions. The result covers compact Hessian manifolds only.
event.revisions: v1 1 Sep 2025; v2 9 Oct 2025; v3 15 Oct 2025; v4 20 Oct 2025; v5 3 Nov 2025; v6 18 Nov 2025; v7 11 Jun 2026 (current). Titles: v1 'On Topology and Geometry of Hessian Manifolds'; later 'On Topology of Compact Hessian Manifolds'. Numbering of the key proposition changes between versions (Prop 2.17 in earlier versions, Prop 4.3 in the later one, per a search summary).
event.delivers: Claimed: chi = 0 for every compact Hessian manifold (a Hessian manifold is an affine manifold with a metric locally the Hessian of a potential). Restriction: the Hessian class only. The general compact affine case is not addressed.
event.remains: All compact affine manifolds that are not Hessian (and not otherwise covered).
event.time_since_posted: About 13 months to Oct 2026. No referee, publication, or public expert reading found in any search.
event.doubts: Preprint, unrefereed, 49 pages, with several versions. The method goes through fibration and splitting theorems; I did not check them. Only the first 100,000 of about 172,000 characters of v6 were read in the keyword check, so the AI and acknowledgement check is incomplete for v6. The abstract's classification results for surfaces and 3-manifolds are separate claims.
event.direction: Claims the conjecture for compact Hessian manifolds: chi = 0 in that class. Direction matches the conjecture in that restricted class.

judgement.why: The statement is a single universal claim, so any proper subclass (Hessian, special, complete, amenable holonomy) is a case. Liu's compact-Hessian result is the cleanest post-snapshot case: credible but unreviewed. The researcher suggested it might be mere 'instances', but it proves the claim for an infinite class, which makes it a case. Casali-Moraschini proves a different quantity (simplicial volume) in the complete case, which was already settled, so it is a variant. The close call is Cocos 2025. It treats the whole problem and is unreviewed. I set it aside as not_credible rather than doubtful because the F10 signals arrive together: no uptake, many rapid revisions after a long dormancy, a hedged abstract, a method aimed at the known obstruction, and the author's abandoned 2015 argument. I dated it after the snapshot as a separate event because the record says the route changed in v4. Its DeepSeek credit covers 'technical calculations' on the key local-metrizability step. That is computation entering the argument, so I scored it assisted, but the evidence is thin. Older pre-snapshot classical results are marked digested as long-accepted literature.
judgement.doubts: The AI role on cocos-2025-revised-route is a close call between assisted and none: the calculations are not described, and the tail of the quote was not confirmed character by character. The not_credible call could reasonably be doubtful; it is the event's credibility, not its scope, that removes it. Many of the pre-snapshot classical events are known only from Wikipedia and secondary summaries; I marked them digested as established literature.
